title: Complete sets at higher levels

based_on.title: Computability theory
based_on.pages: Version 2024-02-25; §17.1 Lemma 17.1 and its full proof, and Corollary 17.3, p.71; the common oracle selectors and positive-level restriction are made explicit

summary: Upgrade ordinary reductions around any oracle jump to computable permutations, and classify complete sets at every positive hierarchy level.
abstract: Totality of a program and infinitude of its domain look like different membership problems, yet a computable permutation can rename one into the other. The reason is their shared completeness at the second universal level of the arithmetical hierarchy. At every positive level, any two complete sets are related by an ordinary computable permutation with a computable inverse, even when the hierarchy is based on a noncomputable oracle. The key is a special property of halting problems: a many-one reduction out of relative halting can be replaced by an injective reduction. Two common self-referential programs escape any finite record of used images, and a bounded finite scan then selects distinct outputs. Padding supplies the opposite injection, and Myhill’s matching construction gives the permutation. Applying this to successive jumps yields the existential classification; complementing the same permutations yields the universal classification. Finite computable sets show why the positive-level hypothesis is necessary.
